Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #126

The change

On macOS and Linux, with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA set, the plugin made its state folders 0755 and its job files 0644. The job files hold your prompts and Copilot's answers. assessment:20

The fix makes the plugin's state folders 0700 and its new job and log files 0600, and tightens its own older folders, best effort. fix:10

2code files fix:18
18tests added, macOS and Linux only fix:20
3checks passed test:21
2checks not run here test:19
2deviations fix:74

Root cause

The owner-only mode was set for the home fallback only; everything under Claude Code's data folder got the default mode. assessment:48

Remediation

Create with 0700 and 0600, and tighten the plugin's own older folders and an existing log, skipping links and ignoring failures. assessment:58

Look-ups

Glossary
  • 0700, 0600: readable and writable by the owner only, for a folder and a file.
  • umask: the bits taken away from a new file's mode; 022 gives 0755 folders and 0644 files.

# Bug Assessment: the state folder and job files are readable by others under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA - **Slug**: 126-state-folder-owner-only- **Created**: 2026-10-27- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #126)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: medium ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Summarized from #126. `ensurePluginDataDir` (`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs`) sets mode0700 only on the home fallback (`~/.copilot-companion`). With `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set, the normalcase, `state/<slug>/jobs` is created with the default mode (0755 under umask 022) and the files with0644. `jobs/<id>.json` holds the whole prompt, the request and Copilot's answer; the log holds theprogress. Whether another user can read them depends on the mode of Claude Code's data folder,which the plugin does not check. A shared Linux or macOS host is the realistic exposure. The issueasks for the plugin's state folder and job files to be owner-only on macOS and Linux, wherever thedata folder is, with a test, a docs update and a patch release. ## Symptom On macOS and Linux, with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set, `<plugin data>/state/<slug>` and `jobs/` are 0755and `state.json`, `jobs/<id>.json` and `jobs/<id>.log` are 0644 (under umask 022). Expected: thefolders 0700 and the files 0600, as for the home fallback. ## Reproduction From the code (this machine is Windows, where the mode does not apply); CI on Ubuntu and macOS runsthe new tests: 1. Set `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` to a 0755 temp folder, umask 022.2. Run any state update and start a job (`updateState`, `writeJobFile`, `createJobLogFile`).3. `state/<slug>` and `jobs` are 0755; `state.json`, `<id>.json` and `<id>.log` are 0644. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs:99-110` (`ensurePluginDataDir`): 0700 only for the  fallback folder.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs:112-115` (`ensureStateDir`): `mkdirSync(jobsDir,  { recursive: true })` with the default mode.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs:412-421` (`writeJsonAtomic`): the temp file for  `state.json` and `jobs/<id>.json` gets the default mode; the rename keeps it.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs:42-62` (`appendLogLine`, `appendLogBlock`,  `createJobLogFile`): the log gets the default mode.- The lock owner files (`state.mjs`, `openSync(ownerFile, "wx")`) hold only a pid and a token, in  the same folder. ## Root Cause Hypothesis The owner-only mode was added for the fallback folder only. The plugin's own folders and files underClaude Code's data folder are made with the default mode, so their reach depends on a folder theplugin does not own. Confidence: high (read from the code). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: - `ensureStateDir`: `mkdirSync(jobsDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })`. `recursive` applies the  mode to each folder it creates, which can include `state/` itself; an existing `state/` and the  data folder keep their mode.- Then, on non-Windows only, the plugin's own two folders from an older version are tightened, best  effort, each in its own `try`. This goes past "create with 0700" on purpose: after an upgrade the  folders exist already, so without it the acceptance "the state folder is 0700" would not hold for  anyone who used the plugin before. `lstatSync` `state/<slug>`; when it is a link, or the `lstatSync` fails  (so it may be a link), stop: neither it nor its `jobs` is changed. Otherwise, for `state/<slug>`  and then for `jobs`, each in its own `try`: when it is not a link (for `jobs`, its own  `lstatSync`) and its mode is not 0700, `chmodSync` it to 0700. A `chmodSync` error on  `state/<slug>` (EPERM or EROFS) skips that folder only, and an error on `jobs` skips `jobs`; the  call goes on: such a folder is open whatever the plugin does, and a failure  would also block the read calls that use `ensureStateDir` (`resolveJobFile`,  `resolveJobLogFile`, `resolveJobPatchDir`), so `status` and `cancel`.- `writeJsonAtomic`: create the temp file with `mode: 0o600`; the rename keeps it, so `state.json`  and `jobs/<id>.json` are 0600 each time they are written.- `tracked-jobs.mjs`: `mode: 0o600` on the log's `writeFileSync` and both `appendFileSync` calls, so  a new log is 0600. The option applies only at creation, so `createJobLogFile`, where each job's  log starts, also tightens a log that exists already: after the `writeFileSync`, on non-Windows,  in a `try`, `lstatSync` it and `chmodSync` it to 0600 when it is not a link and its mode is not  0600; a failure leaves it as it is and the job goes on. The two append helpers only add to a log  that a job has started; only a job that runs across an upgrade could append to an older 0644 log,  which sits in the now-0700 `jobs` folder. A job file of an older version becomes 0600 when it is  written again (the rename).- `ensurePluginDataDir` is unchanged: a data folder that `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` names and that does  not exist yet is created with the default mode, because it is Claude Code's folder, not the  plugin's.- The lock owner files stay as they are (a pid and a token, 0644 under umask 022): they are in the  0700 folder.- Windows: no change. The `chmodSync` calls run only on non-Windows; the `mode` options are passed  everywhere and Windows ignores them.- `docs/configuration.md` "Folders": on macOS and Linux, with or without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`,  each workspace's state folder (`state/<slug>`) and its `jobs` folder are owner-only, also when  an older version made them; new job and log files are owner-only too. The `state` folder above  them is owner-only when the plugin creates it; the plugin does not change an existing one, nor  the data folder itself. The CHANGELOG entry says the same, with the tightening of older folders. The `state.mjs` and `tracked-jobs.mjs` header comments  and a README "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet record the change from upstream, which  makes these folders with the default mode too. **Alternatives**:- Only the folder modes: a 0700 folder already keeps others out, but the issue asks for 0600 files,  which also hold if the folder mode is loosened later.- A process-wide `umask`: it would also change files the plugin writes elsewhere, and it does not  tighten existing folders. **Files likely to change**:- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs`, `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs`- `tests/state.test.mjs`, `tests/tracked-jobs.test.mjs`- `docs/configuration.md`, `README.md`- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (`npm run bump-version -- 1.0.23`) **Tests to add or update** (skipped on Windows; each sets `process.umask(0o022)` itself andrestores it in `finally`, and uses a fresh data folder; mocks match the exact path, not a callcount). These fail on the current code:- With `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` set to a folder that the test `chmodSync`s to 0755: after `updateState`,  `writeJobFile` and `createJobLogFile`, `state/<slug>` and `jobs` are 0700, `state.json`,  `<id>.json` and `<id>.log` are 0600, the fresh `state/` is 0700, and the data folder is still  0755.- The same without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` (the fallback); the existing fallback tests stay.- An existing `state/<slug>` and `jobs` at 0755 become 0700.- `appendLogLine` and `appendLogBlock` each on a log that does not exist yet: 0600.- `writeJsonAtomic` replacing an existing 0644 `state.json` and `<id>.json`: 0600 after the rename.- `fs.renameSync` mocked to check the temp file's mode (0600) and then throw: the update fails and  the temp file is removed, as today.- A data folder that `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` names and that does not exist yet: `state/` and  `state/<slug>` come out 0700, and the data folder has the default mode.- A real `state/<slug>` at 0755 whose `jobs` is a link to a 0755 folder: `state/<slug>` becomes  0700 and the link's target keeps 0755.- `createJobLogFile` on an existing 0644 log: 0600.- `fs.chmodSync` mocked to throw EPERM for a 0755 `state/<slug>`: `jobs` still becomes 0700.- `fs.lstatSync` mocked to throw for `jobs` after `state/<slug>` is checked: `state/<slug>` becomes  0700. These guard against a regression and pass on the current code too:- An existing `state/` at 0755 keeps 0755.- `fs.chmodSync` mocked to throw EPERM for `state/<slug>`, for `jobs` and for an existing log, and  `fs.lstatSync` mocked to throw ENOENT and EACCES for `state/<slug>` (then neither folder is  changed: both keep 0755), for `jobs` and for the log (then the "Starting" line is still written): `updateState`, `writeJobFile`, `createJobLogFile` and  the read call `resolveJobLogFile` still work.- `state/<slug>` as a link to a 0755 folder that holds a 0755 `jobs`, and the log as a link to a  0644 file: the targets keep their modes.- The lock owner files are not tested; they sit in the 0700 folder. **Checks**: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check-version` and`claude plugin validate .` must pass before the PR; CI runs the tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. ## Risks & Considerations - Two `lstatSync` calls on every `ensureStateDir` call, and a `chmodSync` only for a folder that is  not 0700: small next to the git and file work around them.- Accepted limit: a `state/<slug>` or `jobs` folder that is open to others and cannot be closed  (another user owns it, or a read-only file system) stays open, and the plugin goes on writing to  it. Refusing to write would stop reviews there, and the folder is open whatever the plugin does.  The docs say the folders are made owner-only, not that an existing open folder is refused.- A link at `state/<slug>` gets no `chmodSync`, nor its `jobs`, so their targets keep their modes;  the files written there still get 0600. `chmodSync` follows a link, so a folder swapped for a  link between the `lstatSync` and the `chmodSync` would have its target changed; that needs write  access to the folder above it, which is the plugin's own or Claude Code's.- A log of an older version keeps 0644, and a job file of an older version keeps it until it is  written again; both sit inside the 0700 `jobs` folder.- The tests run their mode checks only in CI on Ubuntu and macOS; this machine is Windows. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. Names and layout stay; the safer modes are a difference from upstream,  recorded in the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" and the header comments.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. Node's `fs` modes and `chmodSync`; no new dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. No change to how Copilot is called.- **IV. Safe by default**: met; this is the point of the fix. The plugin makes its state folders and  new files owner-only and tightens its own older folders; a folder it cannot close is an accepted  limit (Risks).- **V. Cross-platform**: met. The mode checks run on macOS and Linux; Windows is unchanged; CI runs  all three.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Fresh and existing folders and files, with and  without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, the data folder and an existing `state/` left alone, logs created by  each writer, replaced JSON files, a linked folder, and a failed `lstatSync` or `chmodSync` that  blocks nothing. Patch release with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the release run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: the state folder and job files are readable by others under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA - **Slug**: 126-state-folder-owner-only- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary On macOS and Linux the plugin now creates its state folders with mode 0700 and its job and logfiles with 0600, also under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, and tightens its own `state/<slug>` and `jobs`folders and an existing log from an older version, best effort. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/state.mjs` | modified | `makeOwnerOnly(file, mode)` (best effort, skips links); `ensureStateDir` creates `jobs` with 0700 and tightens `state/<slug>`, then `jobs` only when `state/<slug>` was checked and is no link; `writeJsonAtomic` temp file 0600; header comment || `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs` | modified | Log writes with mode 0600; `createJobLogFile` tightens an existing log; header comment || `tests/state-modes.test.mjs` | added | 18 tests, skipped on Windows || `docs/configuration.md` | modified | "Folders": which folders and files are owner-only || `README.md` | modified | A "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.23` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.23` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jsexport function ensureStateDir(cwd) {  ensurePluginDataDir();  const jobsDir = resolveJobsDir(cwd);  fs.mkdirSync(jobsDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });  if (makeOwnerOnly(path.dirname(jobsDir), 0o700)) {    makeOwnerOnly(jobsDir, 0o700);  }}``` ## Tests Added or Updated `tests/state-modes.test.mjs` (a new file, so its umask and data-folder settings stay apart; each testsets umask 022 and a fresh data folder). These fail on the old code: - Under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` (a 0755 folder): `state/`, `state/<slug>` and `jobs` are 0700,  `state.json`, `<id>.json` and the log are 0600, and the data folder keeps 0755.- Without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` (the fallback in a temp `HOME`): the same.- A data folder that does not exist yet: it gets the default mode, the folders under it 0700.- Folders and a log from an older version (0755, 0644) are tightened; an existing `state/` is not.- Job files rewritten from 0644 become 0600.- A log that `appendLogLine` or `appendLogBlock` creates is 0600.- The temp file of a state write is 0600 before its rename (a mocked rename that fails).- A `jobs` link: its target keeps 0755 while `state/<slug>` becomes 0700.- A `chmodSync` failure on `state/<slug>` still lets `jobs` be tightened; an `lstatSync` failure on  `jobs` still lets `state/<slug>` be tightened. These pass on the old code too and guard what the fix must not break: - With `chmodSync` or `lstatSync` failing for `state/<slug>`, `jobs` or the log (EPERM, EROFS,  ENOENT, EACCES), state updates, job files, the log and the read call `resolveJobLogFile` still  work; an `lstatSync` failure on `state/<slug>` changes neither folder.- A `state/<slug>` link and a log link: their targets keep their modes. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run build` (pass), `npm test`  (503 tests: 461 pass, 42 skipped, 0 fail; the 18 new tests skip on this Windows machine),  `npm run check-version` (1.0.23), `claude plugin validate .` (pass).- The new tests run only on macOS and Linux, so CI on Ubuntu and macOS runs them; WSL is not  reachable from this session. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27: the mode tests are in a new file, `tests/state-modes.test.mjs`, not in  `tests/state.test.mjs` and `tests/tracked-jobs.test.mjs`, because both set one module-level  `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` that other tests use. The assessment was written in the format of  `/speckit-bug-assess` without running that skill.- 2026-10-27, review round 1: the guard test "an existing `state/` keeps 0755" was removed, because  the upgrade test makes the same check; the tests restore unset environment variables by deleting  them; the docs name the workspace folder `state/<repo folder name>-<hash>` and say that `jobs`  stays as it is when that folder is a link or cannot be checked. ## Follow-ups - None.
